A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NIMO and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably across pagination changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic regression and classification experiments, evaluations on diabetes, Boston housing, and superconductivity, and masking and positional-encoding ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds self-interaction experiments, local-explanation analyses, a group-penalty ablation, and PMLB benchmark results.

M1.justification: NIMO's masked correction networks, shared positional encoding, sparsity mechanisms, and parameter-elimination training remain unchanged. The new basis-expansion experiments apply preprocessing to the existing model.

E1.justification: V3 adds ten PMLB regression datasets, including 197_cpu_act, 503_wind, and 225_puma8NH (Appendix D.10). It also introduces a purely quadratic self-interaction scenario outside the original synthetic model structure (D.6), while retaining the previous datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding original predictive and SHAP-ranking comparisons retain their comparator membership. The added experiments reuse Lasso, LassoNet, NN, and SHAP. NODE-GAM and Interpretable Mixture of Experts are added to related work but are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 changes the stated NN dropout for superconductivity from 0.6 to 0.1. New protocols include original versus polynomial-expanded inputs, a group-penalty control, local-contribution comparisons, and a mean nonlinear-correction diagnostic. D.10 introduces PMLB size filtering and grid-search tuning; these are additional evaluations rather than revisions to all retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained masking and positional-encoding ablations, D.6–D.9 add a self-interaction failure-and-remedy study, local contributions compared with synthetic ground truth and Boston SHAP values, a diabetes/Boston nonlinearity comparison, and an ablation testing the first-layer group penalty.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 9/9/5 seed counts in Section 4.2 and the five-run description with cross-split error bars and confidence intervals in D.4. V3 specifies no increased repeat count, significance test, or revised uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and most original results are retained, but Figures 5 and 13 replace the NN superconductivity results, shifting plotted errors from roughly 0.15 to around 0.10 alongside the dropout revision. New Table 4 reports NIMO values of 5.340 and 1.009 before and after basis expansion, versus LassoNet's 1.027 and 1.012. Figures 17–22 add substantial diagnostic and benchmark findings.

T1.justification: V3 introduces the explicit nonlinearity diagnostic n_j(x) = |1 + g_uj(x_-j)| in Equation 51. The adaptive-ridge equivalence proof, parameter-elimination derivations, IRLS extension, and sub-l1 mathematics in Appendices A–B remain unchanged apart from renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contribution statements retain the same claims about globally interpretable coefficients, per-instance corrections, parameter-elimination optimization, and competitive prediction. The conclusion's self-interaction caveat is expanded elsewhere rather than abandoned.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the inference that differing coefficients demonstrate nonlinear interactions with an explanation involving correlated predictors and unstable feature selection. Section 3.2 adds qualifications about MEM's applicability, while Section 4.4 and D.6 substantially develop the architectural self-interaction limitation and feature-engineering remedy. D.7 also interprets local SHAP agreement and disagreements.

D1.justification: V3 revises the NN dropout specification and supplies the quadratic data generator, explicit nine-feature polynomial expansion, PMLB size thresholds, and a grid-search statement. Existing implementation, hardware, and repository-access information is retained; detailed PMLB tuning grids and experiment-specific split information are not supplied.

R1.justification: Related work adds NODE-GAM and Interpretable Mixture of Experts, contrasting their interpretations with NIMO's global coefficients. New citations also support the MEM limitations discussion and PMLB benchmark. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section ordering are retained. Changes concentrate on the hybrid-model discussion, result interpretation, a dedicated limitations subsection, and new appendix subsections D.6–D.10. Author emails and the conference-publication header are also added.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4 and Figures 17–22, introducing original-versus-expanded-feature displays, local-explanation scatter plots, nonlinearity and penalty analyses, and a PMLB comparison chart. Existing displays are retained with some relocation and reflow, and Figure 14's caption explicitly identifies the coefficients as MEMs.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens evidence about NIMO's applicability: the previously brief self-interaction caveat becomes a demonstrated failure case with a tested remedy, while local-explanation checks and the group-penalty ablation support important design claims. Broader PMLB evaluation and the more cautious interpretation of correlated features improve credibility. New benchmark protocols remain incompletely documented, but the gains in validation and clarity about limitations are substantial.
